summary:
In recent development, the demand for people to perceive sophisticated data through an easier path, especially for people with visual impairments have been growing.

Therefore, we present A5TROVision, a Python program that makes Earth science more accessible and engaging through the use of sound. Focusing on global temperature anomalies from 1880-2025, this program converts annual temperature values from NASA's GISTEMP dataset into tones aligning with a graph, allowing users to hear how global temperatures have changed over time.

This program shows data through audio sonification with an interactive graph and a synchronized NASA Earth temperature visualization. Users can explore points for each year, listen to their corresponding tones, follow changes through playback, and interact with the timeline to examine specific points in the dataset, with extra information regarding the specific points.

Ultimately, A5TROVision offers an alternative way to experience, access, and understand climate information. It aims to make complex Earth science data more engaging, approachable, and accessible, encouraging people to explore more, regardless of their background or abilities, so that everyone can engage and informed with the world around them.
details:
Our project, A5TROVision, is a simple program that helps convert numerical data (from tables, CSVs, and such) into readable, hearable, and much more accessible data.
It uses NASA's data, specifically the global temperature anomalies and means annually to make it more clear on how temperature has changed since 1880.
This project is intended to help make data more accessible and much less complicated, to make it easier for users to understand it. Sound, the main thing about this program, helps make data much more easier to understand even when you cannot see it. It can help people who have difficulties in vision, and still let them hear the changes.

The tools used in this project are simple, only Python. Along with extra installations and technologies (matplotlib, numpy, pandas, pygame, opencv, mplcursors) via pip.

As for the coding process, credits given to ChatGPT for helping in debugging and give syntax vocabulary, as our group consists of beginner-level coders.

Our project integrates visual data into sound, to help people understand changes in global temperature, and make it more interactive. Our team considered the fact that there are people who visually impaired, and how to make data more readable and accessible to everyone not only via visuals, but via sound. Along with that, we also considered our capabilities when it comes to computing and writing code, which is why we resorted to using AI to help in coding, but limited it to only one AI, and avoiding vibe coding as much as possible.

A5TROVision is currently still in its prototype form, therefore it can only focus on checking global temperature anomalies. There will be further improvements for this program.
